newsitem.title: USA: Nissan unveils Frontier, sees 130,000 sold.
newsitem.headline: Nissan unveils Frontier, sees 130,000 sold.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd unveiled its all-new compact pickup truck -- the 1998 Nissan Frontier -- at the New York Auto Show on Wednesday and forecast sales of 130,000 in the first year of its launch.

The Frontier, which is expected to go on sale in November, has not yet been priced, said Tom Orbe, vice president of marketing. But he said the company would price the compact truck very competitively.
Nissan initially will offer the Frontier equipped with a 2.4-liter, 4-cylinder engine. It will add a 3.3-liter, 6-cylinder engine during the 1998 model year.
Orbe said that Nissan expected to sell about 130,000 V-4 trucks during the first model year and up to 150,000 after adding the V-6 version.
The Frontier is bigger, more powerful, a little longer and slightly heavier than its predecessor.
Frontier buyers will have a choice of regular or extended cabs, and 2-wheel or 4-wheel drive.
The 1998 Frontier is the third generation of trucks to be made at the company's Smyrna, Tennessee, plant.
Orbe said the company had no plans to offer a larger truck any time soon.
"For right now we're in the compact truck business," he said. "We are focused on what we feel is a very competitive compact truck, and we feel that that's our strength and our niche in the market."
